thread:
maria: quick sync — ran an exploratory run pairing 4-bit quantized llamaX-40b + speculative decode (branching sampler) against our standard greedy baseline on the multi-hop QA suite. saw a weird pattern: end-to-end QA F1 down ~4 points but token-wise perplexity basically unchanged. anyone seen similar distribution shifts?

 tian: interesting — do you have the run ids and exact config? could be a reranker sensitivity to slightly different beam trajectories.

 maria: run ids: redwood-eval/2026-03/exp-3972 (speculative) vs exp-3960 (greedy). config: int4-llamaX-40b, speculative branch=2, cutoff-prob=0.02, prefill-window=0.8, batch=1. eval harness used deterministic seeds.

 jon: did you enable KV-cache-sharing between speculative branches? earlier we saw stale KV reusing causing token mismatch on follow-up prompts.

 maria: yes, KV-sharing=true, we cache prefixes and then fork caches for branches. I thought that should be fine but maybe quantization + forked KV introduces subtle drift. logs show occasional low-confidence branch swaps near answer spans.

 lena: can you paste a short example where the final answer diverged? even 1-2 examples help.

 maria: sure — example question: "Which treaty ended the 18th-century conflict between X and Y?" greedy -> correct treaty name. speculative -> truncated clause then a wrong decade. snippet: ```spec branch1: "...leading to the Treaty of Z in 1799." final: "...Treaty of Z in the 1880s."``` timestamps and tokenization align but numeric token decode changed.

 kevin: number hallucinations smell like quant rounding altering logits near numeric tokens. speculative decode multiplies small differences across branch merges. maybe int4 kernel's softmax precision truncates low-prob tokens.

 tian: suggestion: run ablation w/ (A) no KV-share (isolated branches), (B) higher cutoff-prob 0.05, (C) int8 instead of int4, (D) speculative depth=1. That should isolate whether branching or quantization drives it.

 maria: I'm spinning them up. baseline: exp-3960 repeated for control. scheduling note: these are heavy - can ops-bot give ETA on a spare 3090 pool for quick runs?

 ops-bot: queued job request from maria. est start: 2026-03-21T14:12Z, expected completion ~30m per ablation run (4 runs). Allocated pool: dev-gpu-small.

 jon: also add a rerank-only postprocess run: keep speculative generations but force the greedy reranker to pick best answer via high-temp scoring on full precision logits (float32) to check if reranker rescues quality.

 maria: good call — added run (exp-3975) with local float32 rerank.

 lena: when you have metric diffs, please compute per-type breakdown: numeric answers, dates, multi-hop link chains. my hypothesis: numeric/date tokens are fragile under int4 + branching.

 kevin: FYI, I ran a toy with int4 + speculative on a toy date-fill set and saw error mode: off-by-80 year drift. pushing more bits to exponent helps.

 tian: we should also log logit deltas at branch points. add option --dump-branch-logits for 50 worst examples. that will show whether quantization flips top-2 order often.

 maria: done. will collect 50 worst. initial quick results: (A) no-KV-share regained ~2 points F1, (B) cutoff=0.05 regained ~1.5, (C) int8 matched baseline, (D) depth=1 regained ~1.8. rerank float32 (exp-3975) fully recovered baseline accuracy for most cases.

 jon: so branching + KV-sharing + int4 is the combo. rerank fix is promising operationally — cheap patch while we investigate long term.

 kevin: ops note: rerank with float32 increases CPU cost for postprocessing ~1.2x but token costs unchanged. should be ok as a temporary mitigation.

 lena: next steps: (1) expand ablation sample to 5k queries, (2) add confidence gating to speculative (only branch when top1-top2 gap < threshold), (3) file an upstream quant-kernel issue with logs attached.

 maria: scheduling those. also experiment idea: "soft-prefetch" where prefix cache is stored in higher precision (fp16) even if model runs int4. could reduce drift. anyone tried that?

 tian: we prototyped soft-prefetch months ago; it helps with long prefix fidelity. cost is modest memory bump. worth trying.

 maria: ok i'll add soft-prefetch run to the queue after ablations.

 jon: thanks — please drop a short summary with run IDs back here when you have aggregated numbers. will coordinate with release to avoid enabling speculative+int4 by default until we have mitigation.

 maria: will do. TL;DR so far: root cause likely interplay of int4 rounding + KV-sharing across speculative branches; fastest mitigation is float32 rerank or raising cutoff probability. longer term: soft-prefetch + kernel fix.

 ops-bot: job updates — exp-3972 -> completed, exp-3973/3974/3975 queued, exp-3976 (no-KV) running on dev-gpu-07.
